| **Field Winding Connection** | Connected in series with the external circuit [1]. | Connected in parallel with the external circuit [1]. | Employs two field windings: one in series and another in parallel with the load [2]. |
| **Voltage Regulation** | Has very poor voltage regulation under changing load [1]. | An increase in load causes a decrease in output voltage, and a decrease in load causes an increase in output voltage [1]. | The output is relatively constant, even with changes in the load [2]. |
| **Aircraft Usage** | Never employed as an airplane generator due to poor regulation [1]. | Used in airplanes; field windings are connected in shunt or compound formats [1]. | Used in airplanes; the arrangement takes advantage of both series and parallel characteristics [2]. |
| **Voltage Control** | A field rheostat is shown in parallel with part of the field winding circuit to control current [1]. | Output voltage can be controlled by a rheostat inserted in series with the field windings [1]. | N/A |
